name: Bayou Eats: Restaurants
subtitle: Po-Boys, Boudin & Oysters
description:
Louisiana's restaurants, from a dressed roast beef po-boy to hot boudin at a Scott meat market.

Bayou Eats is a free guide to eating in Louisiana: 7 po-boy shops, 10 old-line Creole dining rooms, 8 boudin and cracklin stops, 10 oyster bars and boiled seafood places and 7 beignet and sweets shops we checked by hand, plus 11,338 restaurants, cafés, bars and bakeries in 329 towns, from New Orleans and Baton Rouge to Lafayette, Lake Charles and Shreveport. No account, no ads.

LOUISIANA GUIDES
• Po-Boys: dressed or plain, from Uptown to the backstreets of Metairie.
• Old-Line Creole Dining Rooms: the French Quarter and beyond.
• Boudin & Cracklins: stops on Acadiana's boudin trail.
• Oyster Bars & Boiled Seafood: raw and charbroiled oysters, and boiled crawfish.
• Beignets & Sweets: beignets and what goes with them.
• MICHELIN & James Beard: the MICHELIN Guide's starred restaurants, Bib Gourmands and Recommended places, and James Beard honorees (41 places).

FIND IT FAST
• Sort by distance, or browse the map by guide.
• Search by name, town, street or dish: "po-boy metairie", "boudin", "charbroiled oysters".
• Filter by town or cuisine, or hide chains.
• Save places, and find hand-checked places from iPhone search (Spotlight).

LIVE DETAILS FROM APPLE MAPS
Tap "Ratings, hours & photos" on any place to open Apple Maps' own place card, with current hours, photos, ratings and directions.

HOW THE LISTS ARE BUILT
Every guide place was checked by hand in fall 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source: a dated local guide or news story, an official tourism listing or the place's own site. The rest come from Overture Maps open data, kept by a reliability rule tested against New Orleans' business licenses and East Baton Rouge's business registrations, plus licensed restaurants and bars the map data missed. The Department of Health's reports carry no score or grade and aren't published as data, so each place links its own inspection search. Website links are checked too. Nothing is ranked by star ratings, and the app computes no grades. Newer restaurant data downloads from the Bayou Eats website when there is some.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no tracking, no ads. Your location, if you share it, only sorts lists on your device. Saved places stay on your device.

Places open and close, so check before you go. Spot a mistake? Email nick@eatsranked.com.

An independent app, not affiliated with any restaurant, chain or government agency (including the State of Louisiana, the Louisiana Department of Health, the City of New Orleans or East Baton Rouge Parish), or with the MICHELIN Guide or the James Beard Foundation. MICHELIN and the MICHELIN Guide are trademarks of Michelin. James Beard Foundation and James Beard Award are trademarks of the James Beard Foundation. Place data from Overture Maps Foundation (CDLA Permissive 2.0) and others; sources and licenses are on the About tab.

reviewNotes:
1. Purpose and audience: Bayou Eats is a free guide to restaurants in Louisiana (the U.S. state). Its focus is the state's own food: 7 po-boy shops, 10 old-line Creole dining rooms, 8 boudin stops, 10 oyster bars and 7 beignet shops, each checked by hand in fall 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source, plus 41 MICHELIN Guide and James Beard honorees. It also lists 11,338 restaurants, cafés and bars in 329 towns from open map data, checked against New Orleans' business licenses. It is for residents and visitors deciding where to eat, with no ads, account or tracking.

2. How to use it (no login, no setup, no sample files needed):
- Home → Po-Boys (or Old-Line Creole Dining Rooms, Boudin & Cracklins, Oyster Bars & Boiled Seafood, Beignets & Sweets, MICHELIN & James Beard, Oldest Places, Near Me) → tap any place.
- On a place, tap "Ratings, hours & photos" to open Apple Maps' own place card through MapKit. Directions, Call and Website are below it; further down, a link opens the Louisiana Department of Health's inspection search in Safari.
- Search from the Home search box by name, town, street or dish ("po-boy metairie", "boudin", "charbroiled oysters").
- The Map tab shows each guide as pins. "My location" and the Nearest sort use location only if allowed, on the device.
- The heart saves a place on the device (Saved tab). The About tab lists the sources, licenses and the independence statement.
- On iPad, a sidebar replaces the tabs; a place opens in the right-hand column.
- Location: if you're outside Louisiana (as App Review usually is), the map says so and stays on Louisiana, and distance sorting still works from where you are.
- "Bayou Eats" is the Home Screen name of "Bayou Eats: Restaurants".

3. External services and data:
- Apple MapKit: maps, local search to find a place's Apple Maps listing, and Apple's place card for live hours, photos and ratings.
- Core Location: optional, on-device only, for distance sorting.
- Data updates: at most once a day, the app checks the Bayou Eats website (static files on GitHub Pages) for newer restaurant data and downloads it if there is some. The requests carry no identifiers or location.
- No backend, accounts, analytics, advertising, payments or AI services. The restaurant data is bundled in the app.
- Bundled data sources: Overture Maps Foundation open place data (CDLA Permissive 2.0 and others; license texts are in the app); New Orleans' occupational business licenses and East Baton Rouge's business registrations (public records); MICHELIN Guide and James Beard Foundation honors (facts only); and our own research of public websites and local news. Inspection reports are not copied: each place links to the department's own public search.
- The website with the privacy policy and support page is static and hosted on GitHub Pages: https://nickstrom5.github.io/louisiana-eats/

4. Regional differences: none. The content covers Louisiana; the app is offered in the United States and works the same everywhere.

5. Regulated or protected material: the app is not in a regulated industry and includes no protected third-party material. The data is open-licensed or public record, with attribution and licenses on the About tab. Ratings, hours and photos are shown only inside Apple's own place card through MapKit; the app stores no ratings or reviews. The app shows no inspection results and computes no grades. Every website link was checked before release, and adult venues are excluded. The app is independent and not affiliated with any restaurant, agency or the MICHELIN Guide or the James Beard Foundation.
